sources.title: The Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) of the Republic of Mauritius
sources.organization: Republic of Mauritius; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical and current conditions; projections and policy targets through 2050–2100.
sources.methodology: National NDC synthesizes sector data, projections and stakeholder consultation.
sources.limitations: National aggregates; implementation often conditional on finance, technology and capacity.

sources.title: Annual Report on Performance FY 2024-2025: Ministry of Environment, Solid Waste Management and Climate Change
sources.organization: Government of Mauritius, Environment and Climate Change Division
sources.temporal_coverage: Ministry performance for FY 2024-2025; reports coastal-risk assessment activities through June 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry performance report summarizes activities and outputs for FY 2024-2025.
sources.limitations: Government self-report; no independent evaluation of risk-reduction outcomes.

sources.title: Coastal Life and Resilience: Diversifying livelihoods and building resilience of coastal communities on Rodrigues Island, Mauritius
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, GEF Small Grants Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: Community-based adaptation project launched in 2015; story reports activities and outcomes through 2020; page date unstated.
sources.methodology: UNDP story reports a 2015 community-based adaptation project and consultations in Baie du Nord.
sources.limitations: Programme narrative, not an independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: DRR (Floods and Flash Floods)
sources.organization: Government of Mauritius, Observatoire de l'Environnement
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports flood events from 2008 through 2024 and summarizes the Land Drainage Master Plan released in 2025; webpage date unstated.
sources.methodology: Official observatory page summarizes past flood impacts and Land Drainage Master Plan zones and recommendations.
sources.limitations: Summary page, not the plan's technical appendices; it says 16 high-risk sites but enumerates 15 numbered entries.

sources.title: Perception of Climate Change Adaptation in Rodrigues Island
sources.organization: Charles Telfair Centre; author Marie Stéphania Perrine
sources.temporal_coverage: Case-study observations on climate perceptions, livelihoods and adaptation; study period and webpage date are unstated; includes a January-April 2018 example.
sources.methodology: Case study using 110 open-ended questionnaires and 12 snowball-sampled key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: Convenience respondents and non-probability informants; not a representative survey, and study date is unstated.

sources.title: Why have water shortages in Mauritius sparked the worst civil unrest in recent years?
sources.organization: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED)
sources.temporal_coverage: Analyst article reports water-protest events in October 2026 and notes protests in response to water shortages since 2020.
sources.methodology: ACLED analyst narrates protest events and water-cut chronology in October 2026.
sources.limitations: Article does not attribute water cuts to climate change; it names cost-of-living pressures and a police shooting.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.19 (printed p.20), section 4.1 Water.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC records prolonged dry months in 2020/21, 2022/23 and 2024/25, compared with episodes in 1998/99 and 2010/11; it attributes increased frequency to climate change.
claims.limitations: Periods are reported by the NDC.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.19 (printed p.20), section 4.1 Water.
claims.paraphrase: The regional climate projection cited in the NDC estimates a further 13% decline in average rainfall by 2050.
claims.scenario: The NDC cites a regional projection but does not state its emissions scenario.
claims.limitations: National projection; district impacts are not specified.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.26 (printed p.27), section 4.9 Poverty and Social Inclusion; April 2025 forum findings.
claims.paraphrase: Forum participants said poverty limits suitable housing and safety-net access; untitled people in precarious high-risk areas face stigma and barriers to post-disaster assistance.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.29 (printed p.30), section 6.1 Differentiated Climate Impacts.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies women, youth, children, marginalized groups, persons with disabilities and people with health conditions as disproportionately affected; unequal access to land, finance, information and decisions compounds risk.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.42 (printed p.43), annex on poverty eradication and social protection.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports a Social Register and 166 cyclone/flood evacuation centres, plus financial and food aid, social housing, and specialized vehicles for people with disabilities.
affected_groups: families affected by floods and cyclones
claims.limitations: Reported provisions, not an effectiveness evaluation.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.8), Minister's statement; and physical p.70 (printed p.55), coastal-risk assessment update.
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry reports 33 coastal rehabilitation priority sites spanning 31 km, with hard, soft and nature-based approaches; the report does not name the sites.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Solid Waste Management and Climate Change
claims.limitations: Priority identification and approaches, not completed protection outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.69-70 (printed pp.54-55), section 3.2.2.1, Coastal Erosion and Marine Submersion Risk Assessment.
claims.paraphrase: Government reports hotspot field surveys and completed GIS risk maps for current conditions and 2050/2100 impacts; stakeholders were trained to use them in June 2025.
claims.scenario: The Ministry summary states 2050 and 2100 horizons but not model or emissions-scenario details.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Solid Waste Management and Climate Change
Bureau de Recherches Géologiques et Minières
claims.limitations: Underlying BRGM reports were not inspected; this claim reflects the Ministry's summary only.

claims.locator: UNDP story lines 19-29, sections on local fish catch and Baie du Nord.
claims.paraphrase: Baie du Nord fishers report a 75% decade-long decline in octopus and reef catches; most of the village's 350 residents rely on the ocean for food and livelihoods.
claims.limitations: Reported catches combine climatic and non-climatic drivers.

claims.locator: UNDP story lines 61-72, community consultations and project activities.
claims.paraphrase: Project consultations found that reduced-rainfall dry months left villagers relying on trucked water and paying for storage; a steadier supply was a priority.
claims.limitations: Findings date to the project period.

claims.locator: UNDP story lines 95-98, participatory coastal vulnerability assessment.
claims.paraphrase: Participatory mapping combined village knowledge and data-rich maps to identify low-lying areas prone to sea-level rise and flooding; it recommended future development at least 2 metres above present sea level.
claims.limitations: The elevation is a planning recommendation, not reported enforcement.

claims.locator: UNDP story lines 103-115, training and livelihood outcomes.
claims.paraphrase: Poultry, agriculture and financial-management training supported local women and families; UNDP reports monthly income rose nearly 40% for 16 families.
claims.limitations: Programme-reported outcome, not an independent evaluation.

claims.locator: UNDP story lines 150-156, household rainwater tanks and policy brief.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports 2,000-litre tanks installed at 38 households, reducing truck-water dependence and increasing water available for gardens and livestock.

claims.locator: Official page lines 8-15, notable flooding events.
claims.paraphrase: The page reports that Port Louis flash floods killed 11 people in 2013; Cyclone Belal caused 2024 flooding, two deaths and damage to infrastructure and private property.
claims.limitations: The page does not provide event-level climate attribution.

claims.locator: Official page lines 31-48, Land Drainage Master Plan high-risk zones.
claims.paraphrase: The plan lists flood-prone localities including Roche Bois, Port Louis reaches, Grand Baie-Pereybere, Flacq, Vacoas, Quatre Bornes, Flic en Flac, Mapou, Piton and Cottage.
claims.limitations: These are plan-identified locations; the page is not the technical risk assessment.

claims.locator: Official page lines 53-61, Land Drainage Master Plan recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: The plan recommends evacuation protocols, accelerated drainage works, improved maps and zoning, and nature-based drainage; the page does not report their effectiveness.
institutions: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Centre
claims.limitations: Plan recommendations, not verified delivery or outcomes.

claims.locator: Research article lines 84-90, generational responses to January-April 2018 rains.
claims.paraphrase: Older planters drew on past flood experience and used canals as prevention; younger planters reported being overwhelmed during prolonged 2018 rains.
claims.limitations: Respondent accounts of one event, not a comparative outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: Research article lines 107-108, constraints described by interviewed farmers.
claims.paraphrase: Farmers interviewed named water stress, saline intrusion, limited technical knowledge and credit, costly inputs, and weak agricultural extension as adaptation barriers.
claims.limitations: Interview findings, not prevalence estimates; study date is unstated.

claims.locator: Research article lines 105-113, adaptation measures and political-divide findings.
claims.paraphrase: Respondents described octopus closures, marine reserves and plastic bans as sometimes imposed; adaptation acceptance varied with local party allegiance.
claims.limitations: Study reports political division, not violent conflict or armed insecurity.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The author reports that party allegiance shaped acceptance or rejection of adaptation initiatives.

claims.locator: ACLED article lines 47-57, protest chronology and analyst commentary.
claims.paraphrase: ACLED counted 15 water-protest events in the week after 5 October 2026; over two-thirds involved violence, including attacks on police stations.
claims.limitations: ACLED does not attribute water shortages to climate change.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ACLED says water cuts prompted road-blocking protests; violence widened after police shot a woman.

search_audit.query: Mauritius Rodrigues subnational climate vulnerability floods coastal erosion water drought named communities report
search_audit.outcome: Opened NDC, ministry report, government flood page and UNDP community story; identified named Port Louis flood sites and Baie du Nord household and livelihood vulnerabilities.

search_audit.query: Mauritius climate change climate-security social conflict water shortages protest violence communal tension
search_audit.outcome: ACLED documents October 2026 water-cut protests and violence, but does not attribute shortages to climate; no inspected source explicitly links climate hazards to violent conflict.

search_audit.query: Rodrigues political party divisions adaptation acceptance insecurity conflict obstruct climate response
search_audit.outcome: The Rodrigues case study reports party-allegiance effects on acceptance of adaptation initiatives; no inspected source states that armed conflict or insecurity disrupted climate-adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Mauritius Rodrigues climate resilience capacity community adaptation coastal mapping early warning water livelihoods official reports
search_audit.outcome: Directly read NDC social-protection measures, ministry coastal-risk mapping and training, and UNDP-reported village adaptation outputs; policy proposals are separated from delivered activities.

gaps: No inspected primary source explicitly attributes the October 2026 water-service protests to climate change; ACLED reports water cuts, cost-of-living pressures and a police shooting, so no climate-to-violence chain is asserted.

The Rodrigues study reports political-party divisions affecting acceptance of adaptation measures but does not identify armed conflict, violence or insecurity; no source directly documents insecurity interrupting adaptation delivery.

The full Mauritius CCDR and BRGM Phase 2 coastal-risk volumes could not be opened by the web reader because of file-size limits. The BRGM claim is limited to the directly inspected Ministry annual-report summary; detailed district-level coastal erosion projections remain unverified.
The Government flood webpage reports 16 high-risk sites but enumerates 15 numbered entries; the extraction names listed localities without relying on the inconsistent total.

Baie du Nord's fisheries and household adaptations are documented in a UNDP programme narrative rather than an independent impact evaluation; reported income and water outcomes are not independently verified.
